name: Soketi
description: A WebSockets server that speaks the Pusher protocol, so applications built for Pusher Channels — Laravel Echo, the Pusher JavaScript and server libraries — publish and subscribe through your own server instead. One app is configured from the generated credentials.

access.note: Soketi has no web interface. Your application connects with the app id SOKETI_DEFAULT_APP_ID, the key SOKETI_DEFAULT_APP_KEY (public, used by browsers) and the generated secret SOKETI_DEFAULT_APP_SECRET (server side only), all in the Variables tab, with host <domain> on port 443 and TLS on.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the host your application's Pusher client connects to.

inputs.name: app-id
inputs.label: App id
inputs.description: The Pusher app id your application is configured with.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: WebSocket connections and the HTTP API applications publish through

secrets.name: app-key
secrets.label: App key
secrets.description: The public key browsers subscribe with.

secrets.name: app-secret
secrets.label: App secret
secrets.description: Signs private channels and server-side publishing; keep it on the server.
